question: The originator of Buddhism, Gautam Buddha, was the prince of which of the following republican states during the Mahajanapada period in Ancient India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shakya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Gautam Buddha, the founder of Buddhism, was born as Prince Siddhartha in the Shakya clan.

• The Shakya clan was one of the many small republican states during the Mahajanapada period in Ancient India.

• Kapilavastu was the capital of the Shakya state, where Siddhartha Gautama spent his early years.

• Gautam Buddha renounced his royal life in search of enlightenment, which eventually led to the foundation of Buddhism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Mahajanapada Period:**

• The term Mahajanapada refers to the ancient kingdoms of India that existed between the 6th to 4th centuries BCE.

• There were 16 Mahajanapadas in ancient India, which were significant political, cultural, and economic centers.

• Some of the major Mahajanapadas included Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, and Avanti.

• **Gautam Buddha:**

• Gautam Buddha, originally named Siddhartha Gautama, was born in Lumbini (modern-day Nepal) around the 5th century BCE.

• He belonged to the Shakya clan, and his father was King Suddhodana.

• Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree in Bodh Gaya and spent the rest of his life teaching the path to enlightenment.

• His teachings form the foundation of Buddhism, which includes the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path.

• **Republican States:**

• During the Mahajanapada period, some states were republics where the king was elected by an assembly of people or nobles.

• The Shakya state, to which Buddha belonged, was one such republican state.

• These states had a form of governance that was relatively democratic compared to the monarchies of that period.

• **Buddhism:**

• Buddhism is a major world religion founded by Gautam Buddha in the 5th century BCE in India.

• It emphasizes the path to enlightenment through practices such as meditation, ethical conduct, and wisdom.

• The religion spread across Asia, leading to the establishment of various schools and traditions, such as Theravada, Mahayana, and Vajrayana.

• Key teachings of Buddhism include the Four Noble Truths, the Eightfold Path, and the concept of Nirvana.
